analogies.explanation: An acorn can develop into an oak; a caterpillar develops into a butterfly.
A glove covers and protects a hand; a sheath covers and protects a blade.
A compass indicates direction; a barometer indicates atmospheric pressure.
An ember can remain after a fire subsides; an echo repeats after the original sound.
An author writes a novel; a composer writes a symphony.
A map represents a territory; a portrait represents a person.
A key opens a lock; a password unlocks access to an account.
A chapter is a section of a book; a scene is a section of a play.
Drought can cause plants to wilt; friction can produce heat.
A scribe works with a pen; a sculptor can work with a chisel.

analogies.relationship: Body part → one of its functions
analogies.explanation: Roots anchor a plant; gills allow an aquatic animal to breathe.
A spark can initiate ignition; a prompt can elicit a response.
Bark is the outer covering of a tree; rind is the outer covering of a fruit.
An infant grows into an adult; a sapling grows into a mature tree.
Food satisfies hunger; water satisfies thirst.
A mile is a unit of distance; a minute is a unit of time.
Marble can be shaped into a statue; clay can be shaped into a pot.
A bee lives in a hive; a monk may live in a monastery.
A thorn can prick skin; a fang can puncture it.
A chorus repeats within a song; a refrain repeats within a poem.
A bird molts its old feathers; a deciduous tree sheds its leaves.
A prologue introduces a story; an overture introduces an opera.
A seismograph records ground tremors; a thermometer measures temperature.
A bud develops into a blossom; a larva develops into the adult form of its species.
A cook follows a recipe; a builder follows a blueprint.
A witness gives testimony; a historian can write a chronicle.
A canal provides a route for a boat; a railway provides a route for a train.
Zest comes from the outer peel of an orange; a husk is removed from an ear of corn.
A debt is settled by repaying it; a riddle is resolved by solving it.

analogies.relationship: Beginning → ending of a natural span
analogies.explanation: Birth and death mark the ends of a life; dawn and dusk mark the ends of daylight.
An orchard contains trees; a library contains books.
An ant belongs to a colony; a wolf belongs to a pack.
Struck flint can produce a spark; a struck match can produce a flame.
A filter removes an impurity; a censor may remove obscenity.
A quote can be selected from a speech; an excerpt is selected from a text.
A grain is a small particle of sand; a flake is a small particle of snow.
A mirage is perceived through sight; an echo is perceived through hearing.
A sundial displays time; an odometer displays distance traveled.
A fossil provides evidence about the past; a forecast makes a prediction about the future.
You retract a statement; you revoke permission.
Bait draws a target toward a trap; a lure can draw a target into an ambush.
A scab forms over a wound; a callus develops in response to repeated friction.
Iron is attracted to a magnet; a moth may be attracted to a light.
A cipher conceals the meaning of a message; a mask conceals a face.
A conductor directs an orchestra; a coach directs a team.
An oven is used to bake; a loom is used to weave.

analogies.relationship: Thing → conventional action applied to it
analogies.explanation: The conventional verb for putting a seed in the ground is sow; for submitting a vote, it is cast.
A fever can signal illness; smoke can signal a fire.
A petal is a component of a flower; a spoke is a component of a wheel.
A monarch may wear a crown; a judge may wear a robe.
A planet follows an orbit; a traveler follows an itinerary.
A lever can be used to pry; an awl is used to pierce holes.
Shivering is a response to cold; sweating is a response to heat.
An appetizer opens a meal; a prelude can open a concert.
An apology can address an insult; a repair can address damage.
Too much confidence can become arrogance; too much caution can become timidity.
You sharpen a knife for use; you tune a musical string before playing.
A cloud contains many droplets; a galaxy contains many stars.
A sieve is used to sift; a net is used to catch.
Permission allows someone to act; an invitation allows someone to attend.
An anchor limits a vessel's drift; a brake limits a vehicle's motion.
Evidence informs a verdict; a symptom informs a diagnosis.
Foreshadowing anticipates an event in a story; an omen is taken to anticipate an outcome.
A fleet is a group of ships; a forest is a collection of trees.
A painter works on canvas; a potter works with clay.
A lullaby is intended to encourage sleep; caffeine can increase alertness.
A lifeguard may need to rescue; a referee officiates a contest.
A skeleton supports a body; a frame supports a building.
A calendar lets you look up a date; a dictionary lets you look up a definition.
The receiver of teaching is meant to learn; the receiver of telling is meant to hear.
A needle is used to sew; a chisel is used to carve.
A marathon especially tests endurance; a sprint especially tests speed.
An icicle is made of frozen water; a conventional candle is made of wax.
You remove a feather by plucking it; you remove a branch by pruning it.
An editor tends a manuscript; a curator tends a collection.
Diamond is noted for hardness; rubber is noted for elasticity.
A century counts one hundred years; a dozen counts twelve items.
Rehearsal prepares for a performance; a draft prepares a work for publication.
The nose detects scent; touch receptors in the skin detect texture.
Honeycomb is a structure built by bees; a web is a structure built by a spider.
Water that freezes becomes ice; water that evaporates becomes vapor.
A comma can indicate a pause within a sentence; a rest indicates a pause within music.

analogies.relationship: Evidence object → specialist who studies it
analogies.explanation: An archaeologist studies artifacts; a paleontologist studies fossils.
A nest holds and protects an egg; a vault holds and protects treasure.
Camouflage reduces visibility; a muffler reduces noise.
A thesis is supported by an argument; a theorem is established by a proof.
A prism separates light into a spectrum; a kiln fires clay into ceramics.
A shell protects a turtle; armor protects a soldier.
A bass voice occupies a low register; a soprano voice occupies a high register.
An invoice requests payment; a summons requires an appearance.

limits: Selector/content checks do not measure human difficulty or establish distribution rights.
